items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Okay, we're into reel two now of Bill Huntington and Charles Sewer.

ctx.x: And if you want to ask me something, Andy Bagger.

Okay, we're into reel two now of Bill Huntington and Charles Sewer. Charlie, maybe you want to amplify a little bit of, now that we've begun to discuss some of the modern jazz players from the 50s and 60s in New Orleans.

Yeah, I won't try to talk about the many, many, but the few who struck me at least as being those who others looked up to as normative, as the real innovators during that time. I guess this spans a period of about 10 to 15 years, and every individual will have maybe a slightly different list, but almost any list I think would have to include Ed Blackwell, who I mentioned before, just an amazing innovator.
